steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Active citizenship means taking responsible action to address community or social issues — it goes beyond voting and includes volunteering, campaigning, and community action. | Key Fact: Formal participation: voting, joining a political party, standing for election, contacting elected representatives, attending public meetings. | Key Fact: Informal participation: volunteering, community organising, campaigning, protesting, signing petitions, using social media for civic purposes. | Key Fact: The GCSE specification requires students to carry out a citizenship action project — addressing a real issue through research, planning, action, and evaluation.
